summary: @factiii/runner is a disclosed remote-agent daemon that accepts remote commands over WebRTC to drive AI/shell actions on the host
details: @factiii/runner is a headless daemon whose documented purpose is to accept commands from Factiii's web/mobile clients over WebRTC/socket.io and run AI coding agents (Claude/Codex) locally, including a local MCP control endpoint on 127.0.0.1 and `/control/<action>` endpoints. The control plane is api.factiii.com (user-configurable via `factiii-runner setup --server`), reached only after the operator explicitly runs `factiii-runner start` and completes a pairing step that stores a JWT and machine-key-encrypted credentials under ~/.factiii-runner/ at mode 0600. No install, preinstall, postinstall, or prepare lifecycle scripts are declared; the daemon does not start on `npm install` or on `require()`. The package also bundles four renamed `frpc` (fatedier/frp) reverse-proxy binaries under vendor/ (linux/darwin x amd64/arm64), used by the documented `share-a-port` skill to expose a chosen local port through Factiii's frps server at $FACTIII_FRP_DOMAIN when the operator invokes that command; the binaries are fetched at publish time, not at install. No scraping of installer secrets outside ~/.factiii-runner/ is present, no exfiltration to a non-first-party destination is present, and no hidden second channel is present. Full-host blast radius is real because the remote peer can drive on-host AI/shell actions, but the capability matches the package's stated product (remote-agent runner) and is gated behind operator invocation and pairing.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
